Executive structural synthesis

Greece's quarterly national-accounts picture is classified as constructive but mixed. Growth Quality: Investment-led growth. Investment Quality: Productive-capital intensive. Competitiveness: Mixed / broadly neutral. Household Demand: Durable-led discretionary demand. External Sector: Export-supported external contribution. Across the five modules, 2 are favourable, 3 mixed/neutral and 0 adverse.

Investment structure & quality

The fixed-investment mix in 2026-Q1 is classified as productive-capital intensive. GFCF stood at 16.9% of GDP versus 21.5% for EU-27. Machinery/equipment plus intellectual property accounted for 57.5% of GFCF, while construction accounted for 42.4%. Total real GFCF growth was +12.1% year-on-year in 2026-Q1. Watchpoints: High intellectual-property share; Strong real GFCF growth.

Productivity, labour cost & competitiveness

The current structural signal is classified as mixed / broadly neutral. On the latest common comparison quarter (2026-Q1), real labour productivity per hour grew +0.4% year-on-year versus +0.3% in EU-27. A newer country-only observation is available for 2026-Q2: +2.7% year-on-year. Nominal unit labour cost per hour increased +1.2% versus +3.5% in EU-27. Watchpoints: Large NULC gap versus EU.

Household demand & consumption mix

The current household-demand mix is classified as durable-led discretionary demand. Real household consumption grew +2.4% year-on-year in 2026-Q1. Durables accounted for 5.9% of nominal household expenditure and services for 56.6% in 2026-Q1.

External sector & trade contribution

The external-sector contribution is classified as export-supported external contribution. Net exports contributed +0.73 percentage points to GDP growth in 2026-Q1. Exports contributed +0.94 pp and imports -0.21 pp. Real exports grew +2.4% YoY while real imports grew +0.5% YoY. Watchpoints: Domestic demand accompanied by import drag.

Methodology and interpretation

The growth-regime, growth-balance and watchpoint labels are transparent A-CLUSTER analytical rules. They are not Eurostat classifications. The report chooses the latest quarter with headline real GDP growth and a sufficiently populated expenditure decomposition. Structural indicators such as productivity, unit labour costs and GFCF may have different release lags; their observation quarter is disclosed explicitly. A reconciliation residual larger than ±0.35 percentage points is flagged rather than silently treated as a complete decomposition.
Data source: Eurostat datasets namq_10_gdp, namq_10_lp_ulc, namq_10_an6 and namq_10_fcs.
